primaryText: Mii tao ni mai na bo
translation: I want to see you
comment: The complementizer is optional.

primaryText: Mi tao na bo
translation: I want to see you
comment: Null PRO in the embedded subject position.

primaryText: Dida sumɔ-ɔɔ e-na bo
translation: Father is reluctant to see you

primaryText: Dida sumɔ-ɔɔ na bo
translation: Father is reluctant to see you

primaryText: Mi hiɛ-ka-nɔ ni ma ya skul gbi ko
translation: I hope to go to school one day
comment: The complementizer is obligatory here.

primaryText: Mi-i tao ni ma na bo
translation: I want to see you

alternatives.form: Mi-i tao ni na bo

comment: The complementizer is optional; the embedded 1.SG is the irrealis portmanteau má.

primaryText: Mi hiɛ-kã-nɔ ni ma ya skul gbi ko
translation: I hope to go to school one day

primaryText: Mi mia-mi-hiɛ ni ma ŋa shinaa lɛ
translation: I tried to close the door.

primaryText: O hiɛ-kpa-nɔ ni o kɔ aspaatere lɛ
translation: You forgot to pick up the shoe.

primaryText: Nyɛ hiɛ-kpa-nɔ ni nyɛ ŋa shinaa lɛ
translation: You forgot to close the door.

primaryText: Gbekebii lɛ nye ni amɛ he shia
translation: The children managed to buy a home.
comment: The complementizer is optional.

primaryText: Dida sumɔ-ɔɔ na bo
translation: Father is reluctant to see you

primaryText: Mi-i tao ni na bo
translation: I want to see you

primaryText: Ameele kai ni e-he wolo
translation: Ameele remembered to buy a book
comment: A pronoun or a lexical noun may be the matrix subject.

primaryText: Ameele kai ni Ameele-he wolo
translation: Ameele remembered to buy a book
comment: Out whether the embedded noun refers to the matrix subject or to a third party.

primaryText: E kai ni Ameele-he wolo
translation: She remembered for Ameele to buy a book

primaryText: Mi kai ni ma he wolo
translation: I remembered to buy a book

primaryText: Mi wa Ama ni e-ya skul
translation: I helped Ama to go to school.

primaryText: Jojo gbekɛbii lɛ hiɛkpano ni amɛ sha tsɛnsii lɛ
translation: Jojo's children forgot to wash the utensils.
comment: The pronoun is coindexed with the whole possessive phrase, not the possessor Jojo.

primaryText: Jojo gbekɛbii lɛ hiɛkpano ni e sha tsɛnsii lɛ
translation: Jojo's children forgot to wash the utensils.
comment: Singular pronoun coindexed with the possessor Jojo.

primaryText: Gbekɛbii lɛ papa kai ni e-he woji lɛ
translation: The children's father remembered to buy the books.

primaryText: Gbekɛbii lɛ papa kai ni amɛ-he woji lɛ
translation: The children's father remembered to buy the books.

primaryText: Jojo kɛɛ akɛ Debo hiekpano ni e-he wolo lɛ
translation: Jojo said that Debo forgot to buy the book.
comment: The embedded pronoun refers to Debo, the local subject, not to Jojo.

primaryText: Aku kɛɛ akɛ e-tao ni e-ya skul gbi ko
translation: Aku said she wants to go to school one day

primaryText: Mi kɛɛ akɛ Debo hiekpano ni e he wolo lɛ
translation: I said that Debo forgot to buy the book

alternatives.form: Mi kɛɛ akɛ Debo hiekpano ni ma he wolo lɛ

comment: The embedded pronoun must be third person, matching the closest antecedent Debo.

primaryText: Mary kplɛ̃no ni e-ya paati lɛ ni Pite hu kplɛ̃no
translation: Mary agreed to go to the party and Peter also (agreed to go to the party).
comment: In the elided clause the pronoun refers to Peter only: sloppy reading.

primaryText: Ajele kpã-gbɛ ni e-ye jweremɔ lɛ
translation: Ajele expects to win the prize.
context: Ajele Thompson has been nominated for a prize without knowing it. She sees a notice reading 'Ayele Tomson is nominated for the Anisha prize', does not recognize the misspelled name as her own, and comes to believe that Ayele will win.
comment: Infelicitous in the context: the attitude holder does not self-ascribe winning.

primaryText: Mi wa Ama ni e-ya skul
translation: I helped Ama to go to school.

primaryText: Mi kenya Kofi ni e-saa shiã lɛ
translation: I urged Kofi to clean the house.

primaryText: Mi dai Kofi ni e-ya skul
translation: I forced Kofi to go to school

primaryText: Mi laka Kojo ni e-kpa akpeteshi nu-mɔ
translation: I persuaded Kojo to stop drinking alcohol.

primaryText: Mi laka Aku ni e-ja e-sikilitei lɛ
translation: I coaxed Aku to share her sweets

primaryText: Mi bi Ayele ni e-ta mi adesa
translation: I asked Ayele to tell me a story.

primaryText: Ameele kai ni Ameele he wolo
translation: Ameele remembered to buy a book
comment: The Movement Theory of Control would pronounce a lexical copy here.

primaryText: Ĩ shi shiã mra
translation: I left home early
comment: Past-tense clipped variant of mi.

primaryText: M-á kwɛ o-hiɛ̃ Hɔgbaa
translation: I will be expecting you on Sunday
comment: The irrealis marker merged with the first-person pronoun.

primaryText: Mi tee skul mra
translation: I went to school early

alternatives.form: Wɔ tee skul mra

comment: The verb is invariant across subjects: no subject agreement on the verb.

primaryText: O tee skul mra
translation: You went to school early

alternatives.form: Nyɛ tee skul mra

primaryText: E tee skul mra
translation: She went to school early

alternatives.form: Amɛ tee skul mra

primaryText: Hejɔlɛ á-hã́ nyɛ
translation: Peace be unto you
comment: Lexical subject: the irrealis marker is a prefix on the verb plus a high tone on the verb.

primaryText: É shí biɛ
translation: He ought to leave

primaryText: Amɛ́ bi lɛ
translation: They should ask her
comment: High tone on the pronoun without the high tone on the verb: neither the subjunctive nor a past reading survives.

primaryText: Mi-i tao má na bo
translation: I want to see you.

alternatives.form: Mi-i tao má ná bo

comment: A high tone on the embedded bare verb, as in a true subjunctive, is ungrammatical.

primaryText: Mi kai ake mi he wolo lɛ
translation: I remember that I bought the book

alternatives.form: Mi kai ake má he wolo lɛ

primaryText: Mi nyɛ mi sha tsensii lɛ
translation: I managed to wash the dishes

alternatives.form: Mi nyɛ má sha tsensii lɛ

primaryText: Mi kpleno ni má ya skul wɔ
translation: I agreed to go to school tomorrow

alternatives.form: Mi kpleno ni mi ya skul wɔ

primaryText: Mi kpaŋ ni má shi mra
translation: I planned to leave early

alternatives.form: Mi kpaŋ ni mi shi mra

primaryText: Aku baa-sumoo ni é-shi wɔ
translation: Aku will like to leave tomorrow
comment: The embedded pronoun must be coreferential with Aku: no obviation, unlike a subjunctive.

primaryText: Yà-á shia
translation: Go home!
comment: The reduplicated final vowel carries the irrealis high tone.

primaryText: Wɔ́ yá
translation: Let's go!
comment: Without the high tone on both pronoun and verb the imperative reading is lost.

primaryText: Má ya shiã mra ŋmɛnɛ
translation: I will go home early today
comment: The portmanteau future is permitted with the first-person pronoun only.

primaryText: E bàá-sla wɔ wɔ́
translation: She will visit us tomorrow

alternatives.form: É bàá-sla wɔ wɔ́

comment: The irrealis marker is realized only inside the future prefix.

primaryText: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ a-bàá-tsí paati lɛ a-to
translation: If it rains, the party will be cancelled.

primaryText: Kɛ mi ye lɛ má jo
translation: If I win, I will dance

alternatives.form: Kɛ mi ye lɛ mi-bàá jo

primaryText: Mi-i tao ni má na bo
translation: I want to see you

primaryText: Mi-i tao ni mi baa-na bo
translation: I want to see you
comment: Future tense cannot be encoded in the embedded control clause.

primaryText: O hiɛ-kpa-nɔ ni ó kɔ aspaatere lɛ
translation: You forgot to pick up the shoe.

alternatives.form: O hiɛ-kpa-nɔ ni ó baa-kɔ aspaatere lɛ

primaryText: È hiɛ-kpa-nɔ ni é ŋa shinaa lɛ
translation: She forgot to close the door.

alternatives.form: È hiɛ-kpa-nɔ ni é baa-ŋa shinaa lɛ

primaryText: Mi tao ni mà le kɛji amɛ bàá-ba a-lo
translation: I want to know if they will be coming or not.

alternatives.form: Mi tao ni mà le akɛ amɛ bàá-ba a-lo
Mi tao ni mà le ni amɛ bàá-ba a-lo

primaryText: Osa kplɛnɔ ni Taki á-tsɛ́ Momo
translation: Osa agreed that Taki should call Momo

alternatives.form: Osa kplɛnɔ akɛ Taki á-tsɛ́ Momo
Osa kplɛnɔ kɛji Taki á-tsɛ́ Momo

comment: A true subjunctive complement with a lexical subject; ni or akɛ introduces it.

primaryText: Osa kpaŋ ni é-tsɛ Momo
translation: Osa decided to call Momo

alternatives.form: Osa kpaŋ akɛ é-tsɛ Momo
Osa kpaŋ kɛji é-tsɛ Momo

primaryText: Aku kai akɛ wolo ni e he
translation: Aku remembered that it was a book that she bought

alternatives.form: Aku kai ni wolo ni e he

comment: Focus fronting inside an akɛ-clause; ungrammatical under ni.

primaryText: Aku lé kɛji bo aloo lɛ ni he wolo lɛ
translation: Aku doesn't know whether you or he bought the book

alternatives.form: Aku lé ni bo aloo lɛ ni he wolo lɛ

primaryText: Aku kplɛnɔ nyɛ ni é-he wolo
translation: Aku agreed yesterday to buy a book

alternatives.form: Aku kplɛnɔ nyɛ ni e-baa-he wolo
Aku kplɛnɔ nyɛ ni e-he wolo

comment: A future reading without overt future marking; overt future or past marking is out.

primaryText: Aku dwɛŋ akɛ è hè wolo
translation: Aku thought s/he bought the book

alternatives.form: Aku dwɛŋ ni è hè wolo

comment: Free reference of the low-tone embedded subject.

primaryText: Aku dwɛŋ akɛ amɛ̀ baa-hè wolo
translation: Aku thought they will buy the book

primaryText: Aku dwɛŋ ni é hè wolo
translation: Aku thought to buy a book

alternatives.form: Aku dwɛŋ akɛ é hè wolo
Aku dwɛŋ ni amɛ̀ hè wolo

comment: The high-tone subject must be anaphoric to Aku.

primaryText: Moko-moko ba-ko biɛ
translation: Nobody came here

primaryText: Jojo kɛɛ akɛ Okoe é-ná-aa moko-moko
translation: Jojo said Okoe didn't see anybody

primaryText: Aku kai akɛ e he-ee noko-noko
translation: Aku remembered that she didn't buy anything

primaryText: Jojo é-ke-ee akɛ Okoe na moko-moko
translation: Jojo didn't say that Okoe saw anybody

primaryText: Aku kai-ii akɛ e he noko-noko
translation: Aku didn't remember that she bought anything

primaryText: Aku kai-ii ni é he noko-noko
translation: Aku didn't remember to buy anything.

primaryText: John é-kee-ee Mary ni é he noko-noko
translation: John didn't tell Mary to buy anything.

primaryText: Aku tao ni é na bo
translation: Aku wanted to see you

alternatives.form: Aku tao ni è na bo

comment: A low-tone embedded pronoun and verb, the past-tense shape, is ungrammatical.

primaryText: Aku mii-tao ni é na bo
translation: Aku wants to see you

alternatives.form: Aku mii-tao ni é mii-na bo

primaryText: Aku baa-tao ni é na bo
translation: Aku will want to see you

alternatives.form: Aku baa-tao ni é baa-na bo

primaryText: Aku ye-ee nii
translation: Aku does not eat

primaryText: Aku he-ŋ niyenii
translation: Aku will not buy food

primaryText: Aku he-ko niyenii
translation: Aku did not buy food

primaryText: Jojo kplɛnɔ ni é ka he wolo lɛ
translation: Jojo agreed not to buy the book

alternatives.form: Jojo kplɛnɔ ni é ka he-ka wolo lɛ

primaryText: Aku tao ni é ka na bo
translation: Aku wanted to not see you

alternatives.form: Aku tao ni é ka na-ka bo

primaryText: Asibi he wolo lɛ
translation: Asibi bought the book

alternatives.form: Asibi e he wolo lɛ

comment: A subject pronoun cannot double a lexical subject: it is not an agreement marker.

primaryText: E he wolo lɛ
translation: She bought the book

alternatives.form: E e he wolo lɛ

primaryText: Jojo he ko wolo lɛ
translation: Jojo did not buy the book
